title: This week in recruiting tools: Juicebox buys Fetcher, LinkedIn Hiring Assistant inside iCIMS, Workday ships Candidate Profile and agents
summary: A consolidation week across the recruiting stack: Juicebox agreed to acquire Fetcher's assets, iCIMS wired in LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant, Metaview went deeper into Workday, Workday launched Candidate Profile plus HR agents, Eightfold appointed a new CEO, and Noon published public docs for driving it from AI assistants.

items.headline: Juicebox announced an agreement to acquire Fetcher's assets
items.detail: Announced 6 Oct 2026 (Business Wire; Axios). Fetcher sold batch sourcing on per-role tiers; Juicebox is a natural-language search tool. Fetcher customers should plan for a migration; see Juicebox and Fetcher in the directory and our sourcing-database switching guide.
items.matters: The independent sourcing category keeps shrinking; AI-search vendors are buying customer bases.

items.headline: iCIMS integrated LinkedIn Hiring Assistant into its ATS
items.detail: Announced 14 Oct 2026 (HRTech Series), two weeks after LinkedIn's 'Hiring Assistant 2' update (TLNT, 2 Oct), which focused on smarter matching.
items.matters: LinkedIn's agent now lives inside a major enterprise ATS, so iCIMS customers get an agent without adding a vendor; the seat and InMail credit model is unchanged. Compare in iCIMS and LinkedIn Recruiter.

items.headline: Metaview expanded its Workday integration for Fortune 500 recruiting teams
items.detail: Announced 14 Oct 2026 (Business Wire). Metaview records and structures interviews and is extending that into agentic workflows on Workday data (Metaview review).
items.matters: The ATS is becoming the control plane for recruiting agents; point tools without native Workday or SAP integrations will feel it in enterprise deals.

items.headline: Workday launched Candidate Profile and a set of HR, finance and IT agents
items.detail: Announced 13 Oct 2026 (Workday blog; Investing.com). Candidate Profile is a reusable applicant profile meant to end repeated form-filling.
items.matters: Portable profiles change the apply experience for the largest employers, and Workday's own agent layer now competes directly for third-party automation budget.

items.headline: Eightfold AI named Joe Korngiebel as CEO
items.detail: Announced 13 Oct 2026 (GlobeNewswire). Eightfold sells talent intelligence, matching and rediscovery to large enterprises.
items.matters: CEO changes at platform vendors usually precede packaging and pricing changes; buyers mid-evaluation should ask about the roadmap and contract flexibility.

items.headline: Noon published public MCP docs, a weekly changelog and switch-from guides
items.detail: Published 14 Oct 2026 (noon.ai/changelog). The docs let Claude and ChatGPT users drive Noon's sourcing and outreach tools from their assistant.
items.matters: First vendor in our directory with public AI-assistant (MCP) documentation; expect 'can my assistant run it?' to become a standard RFP line.

directory: New on BestRecruitmentTools.com this week: vendor-neutral switching guides for teams leaving LinkedIn Recruiter, SeekOut or hireEZ and Gem.
